title: batch vizor: runtime batch defaults + quant harmonizer for unit-econ stabilization
author: Liam Chen
description:
Context: customer signals and our internal econ telemetry show recurring oscillations in per-token cost when workloads mix short chat turns and long completion requests. Existing autotuners pick aggressive batch sizes for short-tail throughput but hurt cold-latency and KV cache hit economics for long requests. This PR introduces 'Batch Vizor' (runtime heuristic + config) and a 'Quant Harmonizer' (profile-aware quantization selector) to stabilize unit economics across mixed workloads.

What this PR does (single-string body): Adds a runtime heuristic that observes recent seq-length distribution and KV cache hit rates, computes a smoothed preferred_batch_size and cache_preserve_score, and exposes those as runtime hints to the scheduler; introduces a compact quantization profile selector that picks between int8/int4/float16 variants based on modeled delta in latency and modeled delta in token cost with safety thresholds; surfaces a new econ telemetry stream (batch_vizor.{preferred_batch,size,cached_hit_rate,quant_choice}) consumed by Optimize and the Console; provides a lightweight CLI 'redwood-econ validate' to simulate cost differences on a representative prompt set; implements safe fallbacks so mispredictions do not expand tail latency beyond configured SLOs.

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime heuristic implementation and unit tests
- [x] Quant Harmonizer model and integration tests
- [x] Telemetry + Console wiring (partial dashboards)
- [x] CLI simulation tool for partner/oncall use
- [x] Docs and release notes draft
- [x] Canary rollout plan (50% of traffic to vizor-enabled hosts)

Motivation: reduce oscillation-driven cost increases (~6-12% observed in customer traces) while keeping p99 latency within SLOs. Avoids one-size-fits-all batch defaults by making defaults workload-adaptive and quant-aware.

High level approach: combine a lightweight EWMA-based sampler with a small decision tree that evaluates (seq_len_p25, seq_len_p75, kv_cache_hit_rate, current_batch_latency) -> preferred_batch_size; run this in-proc in the router module to avoid RPC churn. Quant Harmonizer reads profile metadata (model, hw, seq_len_band) and recommends the quantized variant with a budgeted cost uplift threshold.

Rollout plan: feature gate behind "batch_vizor." env flag; enable on a subset of Dedicated pools and on one hosted region for 72h, monitor econ.delta, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and model quality regressions.

Related: ENG-4291 (unit econ stabilization), ENG-4302 (runtime batch improvements), SUP-8421 (customer incident analysis).
commits_summary: initial batch vizor heuristic and API + unit tests
add quant harmonizer selector and profile loader
wire telemetry metrics + console backend adapter
cli simulator for econ validation (redwood-econ validate)
fix: reduce contention in router sampling path; optimize allocations
docs: explainers for operators + rollout guide
review_comments: Aisha Patel: Please add an explicit safety budget parameter that operators can tune separately from batch size — we shouldn't bake a fixed 1.2x safety margin. (addressed in commit 5)

Marco Jimenez: Can you provide end-to-end latency/cost numbers from the internal replay harness? I want to see worst-case p99 impact before approving. (added replay results to PR description + test harness)
Sven Larsson: Two flakey tests in integration failed in CI initially (sim_cost_pipeline_test). I think the sampling window needs a bit more deterministic seeding. (fixed, re-ran CI)
Liam Chen (author): Responded with replay numbers: median cost -5.8%, 95th cost -3.1%, p99 latency change +0.9ms on small GPU pools. Added safety_budget config and CLI override.
ci_summary: CI ran 1 build + unit tests + integration suite. Initial run: 2 flaky integration tests failed (timeout); after test seeding fix and a small allocation optimization the pipeline passed. Lint and vet clean. Coverage for new packages ~78%.
performance_summary: Canary replay (subset of customer traces): median token cost delta -6.2%, 95th -2.9%; p50 latency -0.7ms, p95 +0.4ms, p99 +0.9ms. Quant Harmonizer picked int8 for 62% of evaluated workloads with negligible quality delta in the synthetic eval harness (BLEU-like metric drift <0.3%).
rollback_plan: Feature flag off -> router stops emitting hints; quick rollback script provided (scripts/canary/rollback-batch-vizor.sh). If we observe >1.5% sustained p99 regression or >8% cost degradation vs baseline, automatically disable via rollout policy and notify oncall.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-11-05 by Aisha Patel after two approvals and green CI. Release notes added to changelog under Optimize section.
release_notes: Introduce Batch Vizor (adaptive batch defaults) and Quant Harmonizer (profile-aware quant selection) to stabilize unit economics for mixed workloads. Opt-in behind flag; can reduce median token costs for mixed workloads while preserving p99 latency SLOs. See docs/optimize for rollout guidance and CLI validation tool.
notes_for_qa: QA should run redwood-econ validate against a mix of short/long prompt sets and confirm that the CLI sim outputs consistent cost deltas vs recorded replays. Verify no p99 regressions on small GPU pools; run integration/it-econ/sim_cost_pipeline_test.go locally with deterministic seeds.
